items.title: Paving a win-win path for China and the West
items.description: In a recent interview with China Daily's Global Lens, Alan Macfarlane, professor of social anthropology at the University of Cambridge, noted that the West has had a strong tendency toward binary thinking since ancient Greek times. In his view, this way of thinking profoundly distorts geopolitical and individual relations.

items.title: 'China Shock' claim misses the point
items.description: A growing chorus in Western media has revived a familiar refrain: "the next global economic crisis could be Made in China". This latest iteration of the China threat narrative, packaged as "China Shock 2.0," misreads China's economic fundamentals and ignores the resilience of the world's most complete manufacturing system, experts and corporate executives said.

items.title: Referential experience for social security in Global South
items.description: Across the Global South, governments face a shared challenge: how to extend social security to populations living through rapid economic, environmental and technological changes. For many families in Africa and Asia, volatile food prices, climate shocks and informal employment mean that a single setback can turn temporary hardship into long-term vulnerability.
